report.source_text: A combination regimen of pembrolizumab (200 mg IV every 3 weeks), trastuzumab (6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks after an 8 mg/kg loading dose), and FOLFOX chemotherapy was initiated. The FOLFOX regimen comprised oxaliplatin (85 mg/m2), leucovorin (400 mg/m2 over 120 min), bolus 5-FU (400 mg/m2), and a continuous infusion of 5-FU (2400 mg/m2 over 46 h) every 2 weeks. However, trastuzumab could not be given due to cardiac pathology in the first cycle. Twelve cycles of chemotherapy were administered. Treatment with trastuzumab and pembrolizumab continued every 3 weeks until disease progression.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma metastasis (to right atrial lesion)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old male presented with fatigue, abdominal distension, and leg edema indicating right heart failure. Initial workup revealed elevated tumor markers (CEA 43 ng/mL, CA 19-9 361 U/mL), ascitic fluid with high serum-ascites albumin gradient and benign cytology, and a large 6.2×3.3 cm right atrial mass near the tricuspid valve on TTE. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed an ulcerovegetating gastric mass, with biopsy confirming gastric adenocarcinoma. PD-L1 expression was positive and HER2 status was evaluated. The right atrial mass was surgically resected (10×7 cm) in January 2024. Although a direct histopathological report confirming metastasis from the excision material was not obtainable from the source, the clinical context and the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma at a primary site with a large metastatic cardiac lesion and initiation of systemic chemotherapy and immunotherapy support the diagnosis of metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma.
